title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 / Entra / Graph
providers.scope_notes: Workload Conditional Access requires Workload ID Premium. Do not treat a token-issuance IP check as universal per-request Graph enforcement.

controls.name: User consent for applications
controls.what: Turns off or narrows user self-consent so delegated permission grants need an admin (or only low-impact permissions for verified publishers).
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > Consent and permissions > User consent settings; Graph authorizationPolicy.defaultUserRolePermissions.permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned
controls.quote: By default, all users are allowed to consent to applications for permissions that don't require administrator consent.

controls.name: Admin consent workflow
controls.what: Lets users request consent they cannot grant; designated reviewers approve or deny, and only Global Admins can approve Graph application permissions.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > Consent and permissions > Admin consent settings; Graph adminConsentRequestPolicy
controls.quote: only Global Administrators can approve admin consent requests for apps requesting for Microsoft Graph app roles (application permissions).

controls.name: Users can register applications
controls.what: Stops ordinary users from creating app registrations (and their client credentials); only Application Developer or admin roles can.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Users > User settings > Users can register applications
controls.quote: By default in Microsoft Entra ID, all users can register applications and manage all aspects of applications they create.

controls.name: Assignment required?
controls.what: Only users, groups or client service principals explicitly assigned to the resource app can get tokens for it; also blocks user consent for that app.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > [app] > Properties > Assignment required?; Graph servicePrincipal.appRoleAssignmentRequired
controls.quote: Users and services attempting to access the application or services need to be assigned to the application, or they won't be able to sign-in or obtain an access token.

controls.name: Enabled for users to sign-in?
controls.what: Disables the service principal in the tenant so no new tokens are issued for that application.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > [app] > Properties; Graph servicePrincipal.accountEnabled=false
controls.quote: To block user access to an application, you can disable user sign-in for the application, which prevents all tokens from being issued for that application.

controls.name: Revoke permission (admin consent / app role assignments)
controls.what: Removes granted delegated permissions (oauth2PermissionGrants) and application permissions (appRoleAssignments) from a service principal.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > [app] > Permissions > Admin consent > Revoke permission; Graph DELETE oAuth2PermissionGrants/{id} and appRoleAssignedTo/{id}
controls.quote: You can revoke permissions granted by admins for your entire organization, and you can get contextual PowerShell scripts to perform other actions.

controls.name: Application policies: Block multitenant applications
controls.what: Blocks creating or promoting app registrations to multitenant or consumer-account audiences.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Enterprise apps > Application policies; Graph appManagementPolicy audiences restriction
controls.quote: Restricts creation or promotion of apps based on signInAudience values.

controls.name: Conditional Access (users)
controls.what: Applies location, device, MFA, risk and block conditions when a user obtains delegated tokens for targeted resources.
controls.setting: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies
controls.plan: Microsoft Entra ID P1 (risk conditions need P2)
controls.quote: Using this feature requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses.

controls.name: Continuous access evaluation / strict location enforcement
controls.what: Lets Exchange, SharePoint, Teams and Graph reject user tokens mid-lifetime on IP-location change or critical events like account disable.
controls.setting: Conditional Access > session control 'Customize continuous access evaluation'; strict location enforcement (preview)
controls.plan: Microsoft Entra ID P1 for location policies; critical events in any tenant
controls.quote: Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, and MS Graph can synchronize key Conditional Access policies for evaluation within the service itself.

controls.name: Sites.Selected and other *.Selected scopes
controls.what: An app consented to Selected scopes has no SharePoint/OneDrive access until an admin grants it a role on a specific site, list, item or file.
controls.setting: Consent Sites.Selected in Entra, then Graph POST /sites/{siteId}/permissions (and lists/items/files)
controls.quote: Selected scopes require an explicit assignment action; an application consented for Lists.SelectedOperations.Selected would initially have no access.

controls_unknown: Licensing for app management policies (Application policies): fetched pages list only role prerequisites; Microsoft has previously tied them to Workload ID Premium, not confirmed here.
Whether 'Assignment required' is enforced for managed identities calling Microsoft Graph (doc covers client apps generally).
Exchange RBAC for Applications license requirement not stated on the fetched page; it does not constrain unscoped Entra grants, which must be removed.

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.0 delegated and app-only bearer tokens. Apps authenticate with a secret, certificate, managed identity, or federated credential.

federation.details: Delegated tokens can be obtained by exchanging an AD FS-issued SAMLv1 assertion (SAML bearer assertion grant) for a Graph token. Workload identity federation (issuer/subject/audience match) applies to app-only and managed-identity paths, not delegated user tokens.

ip_restriction.boundary: User Conditional Access can restrict locations. Workload CA blocks token issuance for eligible single-tenant service principals; excludes managed identities and third-party multi-tenant apps.

lifetime.summary: Default random 60–90 min; CTL can set 10 min–1 day; CAE sessions can get 20–28 h tokens

renewal.summary: Refresh tokens roll over on each use; default 90 days (24 hours for SPAs), max age until revoked, not configurable. Sign-in frequency is controlled with Conditional Access.

administration.summary: Delegated scopes vs application permissions, admin consent, app-role grants, app/service-principal disablement and credential revocation.
administration.conditions: Workload Conditional Access requires Workload ID Premium. Do not treat a token-issuance IP check as universal per-request Graph enforcement.

sso.details: Delegated tokens are issued to users, and Conditional Access policies apply to users when they access apps.

offboard.details: Disabling the user blocks new sign-ins and refresh tokens can be revoked, but issued access tokens keep working until they expire (default 1 hour) unless the app supports CAE.

inventory.details: GET /oauth2PermissionGrants lists delegated consent grants org-wide; issued tokens themselves are not listed.

sso.ui: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy (target users, grant require MFA)

reads.ui: Purview portal > Audit > Search; Activities - operations names: MailItemsAccessed

kill.ui: Entra ID > Users > All users > [user] > Overview > Revoke sessions

offboard.ui: Entra ID > Users > All users > [user] > Account status > Edit > clear Account enabled > Save; then Revoke sessions

token_format.notes: Access tokens are JWTs; GitHub scans microsoft_azure_entra_id_token. Client secrets: azure_active_directory_application_secret (no documented regex fetched).

log_sources.name: Entra sign-in logs (SigninLogs / AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs)
log_sources.notes: Token issuance per user+app; refresh-token redemptions land in non-interactive. 7 days Free, 30 days P1/P2 in portal; export via diagnostic settings for longer.

log_sources.name: MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
log_sources.notes: Every Graph request with AppId, UserId, IP, scopes. Needs Entra ID P1/P2 and a diagnostic setting; nothing retained unless exported.

log_sources.name: Entra audit logs (AuditLogs)
log_sources.notes: Consent, permission grants, credential add/remove on apps and service principals. 7/30 days in portal.

credential_id_fields.notes: Per-token request ID; joins to Graph SignInActivityId
Sign-in that issued the token used
Token issue time; use after revocation is a red flag

lifecycle_events.notes: AuditLogs UserManagement; expected after session revocation (mapping not stated in docs)

anomaly_cues: Consent to application by non-admin followed by Graph mail/files reads from new IP
Non-interactive refresh for the user+AppId from an ASN never seen in interactive sign-ins
Graph calls with TokenIssuedAt earlier than the revocation time
Same SessionId seen from two countries
High-volume Graph reads (ResponseSizeBytes) from an app the user rarely uses

containment.steps: Call revokeSignInSessions for the user; remove the delegated permission grant / user consent; disable the service principal or block the app if malicious; reset password if user is compromised.
containment.notes: Refresh tokens die (few-minute delay). Issued access tokens live 60-90 min unless client and resource support CAE, which revokes in near real time.

sample_query.query: MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where isnotempty(UserId) and AppId == "<app-id>" | join kind=leftouter (union SigninLogs, AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)) on $left.SignInActivityId == $right.UniqueTokenIdentifier | summarize Requests=count() by UserId, IPAddress, UserAgent, TokenIssuedAt
sample_query.purpose: Tie each delegated Graph call by one app to the sign-in that issued its token

calls.reveals: Signed-in user's profile (displayName, mail, userPrincipalName, id); confirms delegated token and identity
calls.rate_limit: Outlook: 10,000 API requests per 10 minutes per app+mailbox
calls.log_notes: Graph activity logs capture all HTTP requests but require Entra ID P1/P2 plus a diagnostic setting to Log Analytics/Storage/Event Hubs; not on by default

calls.reveals: Tenant details, verifiedDomains, assignedPlans; tenant footprint
calls.scope: User.Read returns id/displayName/verifiedDomains only; Organization.Read.All for all
calls.rate_limit: 150,000 ResourceUnits per 20 seconds per app (identity limits)
calls.log_notes: Logged only when Graph activity logs are enabled (Entra P1/P2 + diagnostic setting)

calls.reveals: Signed-in user's mail messages (sender, subject, body HTML); mailbox contents
calls.rate_limit: Outlook: 10,000 requests/10 min and 4 concurrent per app+mailbox; default page 10, $top up to 1000
calls.log_notes: Exchange mailbox auditing (Audit Standard, on by default with E3/E5) records mail access over all protocols including REST; bind aggregated per 2 min, sync per folder. Graph activity logs also capture the HTTP call if enabled.

calls.reveals: Directory users with change tracking; deltaLink for incremental re-pulls
calls.log_notes: Directory reads appear in Graph activity logs only when enabled; no mailbox-style read audit for directory objects

unknown: Whether a given tenant has enabled Graph activity logs (off by default)
Whether MailItemsAccessed sync records are generated for pure Graph/REST pulls (docs tie sync records to Outlook desktop clients; Graph reads land as bind)

detections.title: App Granted Microsoft Permissions
detections.detects: Delegated permission grants or app role assignments to a service principal.

detections.title: Delegated Permissions Granted For All Users
detections.detects: Delegated permission grants (scopes given to a client app).

detections.title: End User Consent
detections.detects: Non-admin user consent to an application.

detections.title: End User Consent Blocked
detections.detects: User consent blocked because the app was flagged as risky.

detections.title: Microsoft Entra ID Anomalous Application Consent
detections.detects: Saved query: a user consented to an app they had not consented to in the prior 14 days.

detections.title: Microsoft Entra ID Graph Email Access by Unusual Public Client
detections.detects: Saved query: a public client app newly reading or sending a user mail through Microsoft Graph (MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs).

detections.title: Azure Microsoft Graph Single Session from Multiple IP Addresses
detections.detects: The same sign-in session ID used to reach Microsoft Graph from multiple IPs by a non-allowlisted app, a sign of token replay.

detections.title: Azure VS Code OAuth Phishing
detections.detects: Successful VS Code (first-party public client) OAuth sign-ins to Microsoft Graph, a pattern used in OAuth token phishing.

detections.title: Anomalous Token
detections.detects: Identity Protection anomalous token risk detections (unusual token lifetime or replay).

detections.title: Applications That Are Using ROPC Authentication Flow
detections.detects: Apps using the resource owner password credentials (ROPC) OAuth flow.

detections.title: Application Using Device Code Authentication Flow
detections.detects: Apps using the OAuth device code flow.

detections.title: Application URI Configuration Changes
detections.detects: Changes to an application reply/redirect URI (AppAddress).

detections.title: Suspicious OAuth App File Download Activities
detections.detects: Defender for Cloud Apps alert for unusual file downloads by an OAuth app.
